canonical_statement: The study aimed to develop a schema-based generative-AI framework that extracts complex hierarchical information from unstructured documents and automatically evaluates the extracted information semantically against a human-generated gold standard.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We present a schema-based framework for extracting complex, structured information from unstructured text documents using generative AI, followed by automated semantic evaluation of the extracted information against a gold standard.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: The project goal was to create an Open Science database of 14 research-relevant HTA attributes extracted in a standardized format to support comparative HTA research.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The scientific goal of this project is to create an Open Science database of a number of attributes of interest extracted from these documents in order to facilitate their downstream use by different stakeholders.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: The development set comprised 8 representative NICE HTA documents, and a human-generated gold standard was created manually for this set.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We chose 8 representative documents as our development set ... In addition, we manually created a gold standard for this development set.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Using our schema-based framework, we extract complex data ... in a single model call, in zero-shot mode, from entire documents (20-40 pages long).

canonical_statement: Claude Opus 3, accessed through Anthropic's public API, was used as the primary extraction model because it produced the most accurate and consistent results among the models the authors tried during 2024-2025.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To make the results as deterministic and reproducible as possible, we set the temperature parameter to zero.

canonical_statement: The extraction prompt had three components: PyPDF-extracted document text, task/output instructions, and the JSON Schema defining the attributes and output format.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: Although the JSON Schema was supplied only in the prompt as a soft structural guideline rather than as a constrained response schema, every extraction output obtained by the authors was schema-compliant.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Nevertheless, every JSON output we obtained was schema-compliant, though we provided the JSON schema only in the prompt.

canonical_statement: The schema encoded domain knowledge using attribute keys and descriptions and, when applicable, type, pattern, and enum constraints.

canonical_statement: The schema specified both leaf-level key-value output constraints and the overall nested variable-cardinality JSON structure.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: During semantic evaluation, the attribute name and its schema description were provided to the generative-AI evaluator as contextual information for comparing extracted and gold-standard values.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: Automated evaluation compared extracted results with a human-generated gold standard, with both represented in the same schema-prescribed format.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: The evaluation algorithm aligned nested output with the gold standard by finding paths to leaf-level elements and matching the paths across nesting levels.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: For list-of-dictionary matching, indication_name was the identifier for indication objects; INN was the primary identifier for technology objects, with brand_name used when no INN was present.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: Presence and value matching were classified as TN when neither gold-standard nor extracted attributes were present, FP when only the extracted attribute was present, FN when only the gold-standard attribute was present, TP when both were present and matched, and FP when both were present but did not match.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: Value comparison first used deterministic exact string matching; values that did not match exactly were then compared semantically using a generative-AI model.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: The generative-AI comparison rubric had four categories: exact match, semantic match, useful match, and non-match; exact, semantic, and useful matches were counted as true positives, while non-matches were counted as false positives.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: When multiple list elements could match, candidate matches were ranked exact greater than semantic greater than useful; ties at the highest rank were resolved with a greedy search that selected the first match encountered.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: Claude Opus 4.6 was used for semantic comparison whenever exact string matching failed, and the authors used it uniformly for the evaluation analyses performed in March 2026.

provenance.prompt_version: @ATOM project macro / literature atom schema v1.0

canonical_statement: The study analyzed extraction performance, run-to-run consistency, extraction time and API cost, comparison with traditional methods, generalisability across models, and transferability across HTA organizations and languages.
